dek: Darwin Falls is the one Death Valley waterfall we cover. USGS calls it the park's highest at 80 feet, and the hike is 1 mile one way.
overview: Death Valley National Park is a below-sea-level basin known for record heat, with snow on the peaks and oases in the canyons.

Darwin Falls is that oasis. USGS lists it at 80 feet and calls it the park's highest waterfall, our trail file puts the hike at 1 mile one way, and visitors have reviewed it. No reservation is needed to enter the park.
fallsIntro: Darwin Falls is the only waterfall we list in Death Valley: one hike of 1 mile one way, and one 80-foot height from USGS.
plan: The outing is the Darwin Falls trail, 1 mile one way. Our directory files it under Lone Pine, about 36 miles away in a straight line. Lone Pine is a highway town west of the park, not the canyon parking lot.
feesLead: The vehicle fee is $30 for seven days, and the park's fee page says visitors who are not US residents can use the same fee. Death Valley's page doesn't show the $100 per-person charge that some other parks list.
access: No entrance reservation is needed, and the park accepts card or digital payment. If cash is your only option, buy a pass before you arrive or use a listed third-party vendor. The fee page lists Furnace Creek and Stovepipe Wells among the places to buy a pass in person.
safety: Heat is the big one. The park's weather page records long runs of days over 120°F on the valley floor. That page doesn't mention Darwin Falls and we don't have a temperature for the canyon itself, so treat the valley-floor heat as a warning for the whole trip and carry plenty of water.
